
---
title: "P11) Develop quality assessment instruments"
link-citations: true
---
Alternative labels: risk-of-bias tools; critical appraisal tools

## Definition and typical features 
These studies develop scales to help health researchers or other interest holders assess methodological rigor, including risk of bias or broader trustworthiness, in a standardized way. Such scales typically use multiple signalling questions with predefined response options, sometimes combined into a summary measure. The development process may combine multiple methods research approaches.

## Boundaries to related purposes

## Typical approaches and corresponding examples 
[Consensus study among researchers or other interest-holders in health research](../approaches/8consensus.qmd): Discussion-based consensus on quality assessment tool for subgroup analyses.[@Schandelmaier2020development]

[Reliability and agreement studies](../approaches/4reliability.qmd): reliability of risk of bias tools for observational studies;[@Kalaycioglu2023inter-rater] agreement of ROBIS and AMSTAR tool;[@Buhn2017the] 

[Review of applied methods](../approaches/9review-applied.qmd.qmd): review practice of assessing risk of bias due to missing evidence in systematic reviews to inform risk-of-bias tool.[@Page2023rob-me]

[Scoping review of methods research](../approaches/11scoping-review.qmd): review of existing instruments informed the development of the AMSTAR2 instrument for assessing the quality of systematic reviews.[@Shea2017amstar]
